title: Top-Performer Relief Points: Computation under Seller Performance Standing
content:
**Computation.** The active points for top-performer relief are the points of every violation recorded on the standing record, less every point reversed and every point already expired, stepped down or relieved on that record. The top-performer relief is those active points multiplied by the top-performer rate of 0.125 and rounded down to a whole point, and it never exceeds the top-performer cap of 2 points. The product is worked to four decimal places before it is rounded down.

The figures are read from the seller's Seller Performance Standing record on the evaluation day.

## Inputs and result

| Input | Value or source |
|---|---|
| Points of every violation recorded | each recorded policy violation's points |
| Points taken out | every reversal entry, and every points-expiry entry — expiries, step-downs and reliefs |
| Active points for top-performer relief | the first less the second |
| Top-performer rate | 0.125 |
| Top-performer cap | 2 points |

Result: the active points multiplied by 0.125, worked to four decimal places, rounded down to a whole point, held at 2 points where it would be higher.

## Worked figures (hypothetical records)

| Active points | Multiplied by 0.125 | Rounded down | Relief |
|---|---|---|---|
| 7 | 0.8750 | 0 | 0 |
| 8 | 1.0000 | 1 | 1 |
| 12 | 1.5000 | 1 | 1 |
| 16 | 2.0000 | 2 | 2 |
| 24 | 3.0000 | 3 | 2 (held at the cap) |

**A record with entries.** Violations recorded for 8, 4 and 2 points (14 in all); a step-down entry of 1 point and a relief entry of 1 point. The active points are 14 less 2, which is 12, and the relief is 1 point.
